# Finding classification

<!-- Generated by `python -m classification.render` from classification/findings.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every finding is classified against public taxonomies and scored with the CVSS v3.1 base
formula. Scores are computed by [`classification/cvss31.py`](../classification/cvss31.py)
from the vector string; CI fails if this page and the source data disagree.

> **Scoring assumption.** Scores describe the same defect in an internet-reachable deployment of this application. The fixture itself binds 127.0.0.1 and holds synthetic data, so its real-world risk is nil; the numbers show how the weakness class would be rated, not what was at stake here.

## Score derivation

`ISS = 1 - (1-C)(1-I)(1-A)`; `Impact = 6.42 x ISS` when scope is unchanged, or
`7.52 x (ISS - 0.029) - 3.25 x (ISS - 0.02)^15` when changed;
`Exploitability = 8.22 x AV x AC x PR x UI`; the base score is the spec-defined round-up of
`Impact + Exploitability` (multiplied by 1.08 when scope is changed), capped at 10.

### FINDING-001 — 6.5 (Medium)

`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`

- ISS 0.560, impact 3.60, exploitability 2.84; 3.60 + 2.84 = 6.43, rounded up to **6.5**.
- Rationale: Requires any authenticated account (PR:L); discloses every other user's notes (C:H); no write or outage.
- ATT&CK: T1213 Data from Information Repositories (Collection).
- ATT&CK mitigations: M1013 Application Developer Guidance.
- Evidence: exploit test `tests/security/test_findings_vulnerable.py::test_001_idor_bob_note_readable_by_alice`; fix test `tests/regression/test_fixes.py::test_001_fixed_idor_forbidden`.

### FINDING-002 — 7.5 (High)

`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`

- ISS 0.560, impact 3.60, exploitability 3.89; 3.60 + 3.89 = 7.48, rounded up to **7.5**.
- Rationale: No authentication on the endpoint (PR:N); a single SELECT is injectable, so database contents are readable (C:H). sqlite3.execute() runs one statement, so stacked writes are not reachable through this sink (I:N).
- ATT&CK: T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application (Initial Access).
- ATT&CK mitigations: M1013 Application Developer Guidance; M1050 Exploit Protection.
- Evidence: exploit test `tests/security/test_findings_vulnerable.py::test_002_search_sqli_returns_all_rows`; fix test `tests/regression/test_fixes.py::test_002_fixed_sqli_neutralized`.

### FINDING-003 — 7.5 (High)

`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`

- ISS 0.560, impact 3.60, exploitability 3.89; 3.60 + 3.89 = 7.48, rounded up to **7.5**.
- Rationale: Unauthenticated read of any file the service account can read, including application source (C:H); read-only primitive.
- ATT&CK: T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application (Initial Access); T1005 Data from Local System (Collection).
- ATT&CK mitigations: M1013 Application Developer Guidance; M1050 Exploit Protection.
- Evidence: exploit test `tests/security/test_findings_vulnerable.py::test_003_download_traversal_leaks_source`; fix test `tests/regression/test_fixes.py::test_003_fixed_traversal_blocked`.

### FINDING-004 — 7.5 (High)

`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`

- ISS 0.560, impact 3.60, exploitability 3.89; 3.60 + 3.89 = 7.48, rounded up to **7.5**.
- Rationale: Any client can mint a valid token for any user without credentials (PR:N). In this fixture the token only gates a read endpoint, so impact is scored C:H/I:N; a token that also gated writes would add I:H and score 9.1.
- ATT&CK: T1606.001 Forge Web Credentials: Web Cookies (Credential Access).
- ATT&CK mitigations: M1013 Application Developer Guidance.
- Evidence: exploit test `tests/security/test_findings_vulnerable.py::test_004_session_token_is_forgeable`; fix test `tests/regression/test_fixes.py::test_004_fixed_session_token_not_forgeable`.

### FINDING-005 — 7.5 (High)

`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N`

- ISS 0.560, impact 3.60, exploitability 3.89; 3.60 + 3.89 = 7.48, rounded up to **7.5**.
- Rationale: The endpoint accepts the source account from the request body with no session (PR:N); a negative amount moves funds out of the destination account (I:H); no disclosure or outage.
- ATT&CK: T1565.001 Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation (Impact).
- ATT&CK mitigations: M1013 Application Developer Guidance.
- Evidence: exploit test `tests/security/test_findings_vulnerable.py::test_005_negative_transfer_reverses_funds`; fix test `tests/regression/test_fixes.py::test_005_fixed_negative_transfer_rejected`.

### FINDING-006 — 8.6 (High)

`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N`

- ISS 0.560, impact 3.99, exploitability 3.89; 1.08 x (3.99 + 3.89) = 8.51, rounded up to **8.6**.
- Rationale: Unauthenticated (PR:N); the vulnerable component is the web app but the data exposed belongs to other internal services reachable from it, which is a scope change (S:C); response bodies are returned to the caller (C:H).
- ATT&CK: T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application (Initial Access); T1552.005 Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API (Credential Access).
- ATT&CK mitigations: M1013 Application Developer Guidance; M1030 Network Segmentation; M1037 Filter Network Traffic.
- Evidence: exploit test `tests/security/test_findings_vulnerable.py::test_006_ssrf_preview_reaches_internal_config`; fix test `tests/regression/test_fixes.py::test_006_fixed_preview_allowlist`.

## Two severity labels

Each write-up keeps its original `Severity (lab)` line, a lab-relative judgement about the
demo assets. The CVSS score beside it is the standardized rating and is the one to compare
across findings; the two can differ (FINDING-001 is High in lab terms and 6.5 Medium in CVSS
because it needs an authenticated account).

## Taxonomy editions

OWASP identifiers refer to the OWASP Top 10:2025 (where SSRF is part of A01 Broken Access
Control) and the OWASP API Security Top 10 2023. ATT&CK identifiers refer to Enterprise ATT&CK.

## Reading the ATT&CK column

MITRE ATT&CK describes adversary behaviour, not software weakness classes, so the mapping is
an analyst judgement about which technique an operator would be performing when using each
flaw. CWE is the authoritative weakness identifier. T1606.001 names web cookies; the fixture
carries its token in a header, and the sub-technique is used as the closest published match.
